candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos II.13 (c. 350 AD)

'Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood' — Athanasius marks tēn ekklēsian tou theou hēn periepoiēsato dia tou haimatos tou idiou (the church of God which he-purchased through his-own blood) as the DIVINE-BLOOD anchor. The 'his own' (tou idiou) and 'God' (theou) co-applied to the blood-purchaser cannot be Arian-accommodated: only one whose-blood-is-God's-own-blood can be the Person Paul names. Pauline-Petrine apostolic-witness to the divine-incarnate's-blood as the Church's purchase-price. Pairs with 1 Pet 1:19 (precious blood of Christ as of a lamb).
